correctness.rationale: The additive group is the trace-zero Hermitian n x n subspace over F_{q^2}, n>=3, with generators rank-one nonzero square-zero vv* times F_q^*. Frequencies are Hermitian classes modulo scalar I; summing characters over isotropic projective points yields lambda(A)=((-q)^n/q)*[sum_t (-q)^{d_t(A)}]/(q+1)-1/(q+1), with d_t the nullity of A+tI. Projective Hermitian isotropic counts and Gauss sums give degree D=[q^{2n-1}+(-1)^n(q-1)q^{n-1}-1]/(q+1). The integer-partition extremization for the disjoint rational eigenspace dimensions gives L=[q^{n-1}(q^{n-1}+(q-1 if n odd else 2))+1]/(q+1), achieved with negative lambda only; odd maximizers are rank-one nilpotent frequencies, even maximizers have rank one and nonzero trace (all modulo scalars). The claimed multiplicities count their respective conjugation orbits. Independent complete Hermitian matrix enumeration at (q,n)=(2,3) and (2,4) checked 512 and 65,536 frequency matrices, extrema, degree, and all claimed equality counts. A finite test does not establish arbitrary q/n.

originality.rationale: Classical Hermitian rank-metric translation schemes give eigenvalues grouped solely by ordinary rank of frequency for unrestricted Hermitian rank-one differences. The submitted generator set additionally enforces square zero and trace zero, breaking that scheme into nullity patterns of the entire rational spectral pencil. A published sharp ordinary-matrix nilpotent Cayley walk has eigenline statistics for M_n(F_q), while the symmetric isotropic Veronese example is a different bilinear form and only dimension three in odd characteristic. None implies this Hermitian traceless parity-switching extremal absolute eigenvalue and equality classification by substitution.

value.rationale: The exact nontrivial absolute Fourier radius determines the optimal normalized l2 contraction of a natural Hermitian nilpotent random walk, including a genuine matrix-size parity switch in extremizing frequency character type. The negative extremal modes and equality multiplicities convey structural harmonic analysis, rather than just an isolated finite spectrum.

limitations: Full multiplicity distribution away from extreme eigenvalues is not asserted.
Spectral contraction is for counting-measure Cayley walk, not a general mixing-time equality at every state.
